data.title: US energy firms add rigs; count highest since April 2024 - Baker Hughes
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - US energy firms this week added rigs for a second time in five weeks, energy services firm Baker Hughes ( BKR ) said in its closely followed report on Friday.

The total oil and gas rig count, an early indicator of future output, rose by six to 607 in the week to November 20, its highest since April 26, 2024.

Baker Hughes ( BKR ) said this week's increase puts the total rig count up 53 rigs, or 9.6% above this time last year.

Baker Hughes ( BKR ) said oil rigs rose by six to 469 this week, their highest since May 2025, while gas rigs rose by one to 128, and other miscellaneous rigs fell by one to 10.

The oil and gas rig count declined by 7% in 2025, 5% in 2024, and 20% in 2023 as lower US oil prices prompted energy firms to focus more on boosting shareholder returns and paying down debt rather than increasing output.

But now with spot US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude prices expected to rise in 2026 for the first time in four years due to supply disruptions from the Iran war, the US Energy Information Administration (EIA) projected that crude output will rise from a record 13.7 million barrels per day (bpd) in 2025 to 13.9 million bpd in 2026, while seeing gas output jumping from a record 107.6 billion cubic feet per day (bcfd) in 2025 to 113.0 bcfd in 2026.

The Middle East conflict has caused the biggest disruption ever to global oil and gas trade and could cut world oil demand by more than 4% by 2035 if governments accelerate electrification, efficiency and fuel-switching measures in response, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Thursday.

(Reporting by Vedika Thorat in Bengaluru; Editing by Chris Reese and David Gregorio)

data.title: Nvidia's share slide knocks it below Alphabet in valuation
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Nvidia ( NVDA ), the centerpiece of Wall Street's AI trade, slipped behind Google parent Alphabet to become the fourth-most valuable US company on Friday, as a prolonged selloff in the chipmaker's shares reshuffled the top of the market-value rankings.

The stock, last down 3% and valued at $3.4 trillion, was on course for a seventh straight weekly decline, its longest losing streak since 2008.

The slide comes days after Nvidia's ( NVDA ) first earnings report since co-founder Jensen Huang's resignation, which failed to ease investor concerns about leadership and the durability of AI spending.

Nvidia's ( NVDA ) fall down the market-value rankings also underscores a shift within the AI trade, as investors gravitate toward companies that pair heavy AI investment with established cloud and software revenue streams.

Apple ( AAPL ), seen as less exposed to the AI trade, remained well ahead with a market value of $5.08 trillion. Microsoft ( MSFT ) ranked second at $3.72 trillion, followed by Alphabet at $3.44 trillion, according to LSEG data.

(Reporting by Medha Singh in Bengaluru; Editing by Joyjeet Das)

data.title: Fed's Cook says rate hikes needed to lower high inflation
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook on Friday made a case for more interest rate hikes, saying the US central bank's current policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels she views with "great concern."

"In a different environment, the (Federal Open Market) Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury," given how high inflation is and for how long it has been above the Fed's 2% target, Cook said in the text of a speech to be presented at a central bank conference in Chile.

Cook said the quarter-percentage-point rate hike the Fed delivered at its September 15-16 policy meeting was not enough to moderate current levels of inflation.

What's more, "inflation data received since the September rate increase, including reports last week, fail to provide me with sufficient evidence that inflation is returning to a sustainable path," she said. "There is little evidence inflation is declining."

Cook, who voted for a rate hike at that meeting, was one of two Fed officials who dissented over the Fed's decision last month to leave its policy rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Officials at the October 27-28 meeting signaled that inflation remained too high then even as they refrained from action.

Regarding her dissent in October, Cook said, "My vote reflected the urgency I feel to tackle inflation," which "has been above target for more than five and a half years, and every additional day poses greater risk that price- and wage-setters will adjust their inflation expectations upward."

RATE HIKE EXPECTED IN DECEMBER

A wide range of Fed officials in recent weeks have signaled support for more rate hikes, and financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise rates at its December 8-9 meeting and to follow that move with more increases next year.

Most Fed officials have made a case for gradual action to lower inflation, arguing that doing so would give the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs. But some, concerned with the most recent inflation data, have speculated that aggressive moves may be needed to bring price pressures to heel.

Cook on Friday said the risk of not acting fast enough to lower inflation could bring more pain later.

"Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve," she said. "If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later to catch up, which could increase stress on our financial system and have unnecessarily damaging effects on American households."

The Fed governor noted that financial conditions remain accommodative and are not providing the needed level of restraint on the economy.

Cook, however, was upbeat on the economy. She said growth is "strong and accelerating" and that the job market remains "solid."

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: SRX Global Provides Update on Engineered T-Cell Strategy Following Pfizer–Starna Licensing Agreement
data.description:
Pfizer’s $330 million upfront commitment to three pre-IND in vivo CAR-T programs highlights pharmaceutical industry interest in next-generation engineered T-cell platforms

SRX’s pending acquisition of CERo Therapeutics ( CERO ) provides exposure to CER-1236, a clinical-stage engineered T-cell therapy with seven patients dosed in the ongoing Phase 1/1b CERTAIN-T trial

NORTH PALM BEACH, Fla., Nov. 20, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SRX Global Inc. ( SRXH ) (the “Company” or “SRX”), an AI-enabled platform dedicated to generating long-term shareholder value through investments in high-conviction operating companies and strategic assets, today commented on recent industry activity in engineered T-cell therapies following the November 18, 2026 announcement by Pfizer Inc. (“Pfizer”) of an exclusive licensing agreement with Starna Therapeutics (“Starna”), and provided an update on its pending acquisition of CERo Therapeutics ( CERO ), the operating subsidiary of CERo Therapeutics Holdings, Inc. ( CERO ) , an innovative cellular immunotherapy company advancing engineered T cell therapeutics designed to engage phagocytic mechanisms.

According to Pfizer’s announcement, the agreement covers three pre-IND in vivo chimeric antigen receptor T-cell (“CAR-T”) programs focused on treating autoimmune diseases. Starna will receive an upfront payment of $330 million and is eligible to receive up to $2.3 billion in development and commercial milestone payments, as well as royalties on net sales of approved products. Pfizer also obtained rights to Starna’s technology in inflammation and immunology and in oncology. SRX and CERo are not parties to, and have no involvement in, the Pfizer–Starna agreement.

CERo’s approach differs in technology, therapeutic focus and stage of development. Its lead investigational product candidate, CER-1236, is being evaluated in patients with hematologic malignancies in the ongoing Phase 1/1b CERTAIN-T trial. CER-1236 is based on CERo’s proprietary Chimeric Engulfment Receptor T cell (“CER-T”) platform, which is designed to integrate characteristics of innate and adaptive immunity into a single therapeutic construct intended to engage multiple immune mechanisms against cancer.

“Pfizer’s agreement with Starna is a clear signal that large pharmaceutical companies continue to commit significant capital to differentiated engineered T-cell platforms, even before those programs reach the clinic,” said Kent Cunningham, Chief Executive Officer of SRX Global ( SRXH ). “CERo’s technology and indications are different, and we do not view this transaction as a valuation benchmark for CERo. What it does reinforce is our conviction in the long-term strategic importance of this field. CER-1236 is already being evaluated in patients, and our focus remains on supporting the CERo team as it advances the CERTAIN-T trial and on working toward closing the proposed acquisition.”

On November 3, 2026, CERo announced that it had dosed the seventh patient in CERTAIN-T, the fourth patient in the trial’s second cohort. CERo reported no dose-limiting toxicities (“DLTs”) in the three previously treated second-cohort patients during the DLT assessment period, and has reported expansion of infused CER-1236 cells following administration. In its June 2026 update, CERo reported that the observed safety profile remained consistent with earlier findings of no cytokine release syndrome, immune effector cell-associated neurotoxicity syndrome, DLTs or treatment-related severe adverse events during the DLT assessment window. CERo has also expanded its clinical trial sites, including the activation of the University of California, Davis, which also serves as the primary manufacturing site for CER-1236. These clinical results are preliminary, are based on a limited number of patients, and are not sufficient to establish the safety or efficacy of CER-1236.

On October 7, 2026, SRX announced that it had entered into a definitive purchase agreement under which CERo Therapeutics ( CERO ) will become a wholly owned subsidiary of SRX Global ( SRXH ).

About the CERTAIN-T Trial
The first-in-human, multicenter, open-label Phase 1/1b CERTAIN-T study is designed to evaluate the safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, and preliminary clinical activity of CER-1236 in patients with hematologic malignancies. The study initially enrolled patients with acute myeloid leukemia (“AML”), including relapsed/refractory AML, measurable residual disease AML, and newly diagnosed TP53-mutated AML, and the protocol has since been amended to include transfusion-dependent myelodysplastic syndromes (“TD-MDS”), high-risk myelodysplastic syndromes (“HR-MDS”), and post-JAK inhibitor myelofibrosis (“MF”). Primary endpoints include safety and tolerability. Secondary endpoints include pharmacokinetics and measures of clinical response, including overall response rate (“ORR”), complete response (“CR”), composite complete response (“cCR”), and measurable residual disease (“MRD”).

data.title: US STOCKS-S&P 500, Dow on track for correction as Anthropic retreat weighs on AI stocks
data.description:

* Anthropic down 12.5% a day after debut

* Intuit down after company cuts revenue forecast, agrees to sell unit

(Updates to midday trading levels, adds analyst comments)

By Utkarsh Hathi and Ragini Mathur

Nov 20 (Reuters) - The S&P 500 and the Dow were on track for a correction on Friday as Anthropic shares retreated after a blockbuster debut, dashing hopes that the listing would stabilize an AI trade already shaken by valuation concerns.

Both benchmarks were down 10% from their record closing highs. An index falling 10% or more below its record high on a close-to-close basis is called a correction.

Anthropic shares tumbled 12.5% after surging more than 17% on Thursday in their highly anticipated market debut.

The IPO, together with Nvidia's ( NVDA ) earnings this week, was seen as a key gauge of whether confidence in AI-linked stocks could recover after weeks of selling pressure due to concerns about elevated borrowing costs, regulatory uncertainty following Democrats' victory in the US midterm elections and the departure of Nvidia ( NVDA ) CEO Jensen Huang.

"Anthropic is so critical in assessing the overall market landscape in the end," said Gina Martin Adams, chief market strategist at HB Wealth.

"You absolutely need to continue to see adoption and some form of price discovery as to what companies and individuals will be willing to pay for this technology ... until you get to a point where the market feels a little bit more confident that we've adequately priced it."

The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index shed 8.6% to a seven-month low. Nvidia ( NVDA ) fell 7% to its lowest level since June 2025 and was heading for its longest weekly losing streak since 2008.

Among hyperscalers, Amazon ( AMZN ) was down 2% and Meta declined 3.6%, while Alphabet gained 1%. Amazon ( AMZN ) and Alphabet are among Anthropic's biggest investors.

Neocloud firms CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nebius also dropped over 10% each.

The main US stock indexes were on track for their steepest weekly decline since April 2025, when US President Donald Trump announced Liberation Day tariffs.

Six of the 11 major S&P 500 sectors were lower, with the benchmark heading for its longest losing streak since February 2020.

The tech sector led losses with a 4.5% drop, while industrials and consumer discretionary slipped over 1.5% each.

Healthcare stocks were up 0.8% after four straight sessions of losses.

At 12:11 p.m. ET, the Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 206.90 points, or 0.42%, to 48,890.16, the S&P 500 lost 135.15 points, or 1.88%, to 7,040.68 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 789.22 points, or 3.30%, to 23,091.82.

"Furthermore, waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve. If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later to catch up, which could increase stress on our financial system and have unnecessarily damaging effects on American households."

Cook said that she remains frustrated that inflation continues to rise due to shocks and has been elevated for an extended period of time that leaves the FOMC with the need to act.

"In a different environment, the Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury," Cook said in prepared remarks. "I am skeptical that September's single 1/4 point rate increase will be enough to change the path of inflation."

Looking ahead, Cook said that the pace of rate increases should depend on how the economy reacts to the tight policy but said that recent inflation reports have not shown that policy is not having the desired impact of bringing inflation down to a sustainable path.

data.title: Frontgrade Technologies Help Power Critical Computing and Electronics Aboard NASA’s Roman Space Telescope
data.description:
Frontgrade processors and radiation-hardened microelectronics support critical spacecraft and instrument functions on NASA’s flagship astrophysics mission

GOTHENBURG, Sweden--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Frontgrade today announced that technologies from across its space electronics portfolio are supporting multiple mission-critical systems aboard NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope, which successfully launched on August 30, 2026.

Roman is NASA’s flagship astrophysics observatory designed to investigate dark energy, discover exoplanets and explore the evolution of the universe. Its onboard electronics include radiation-hardened processors and microelectronics, providing critical processing, communications, power-management and control functions across the spacecraft.

At the centre of Roman’s computing architecture are Frontgrade Gaisler’s GR740 and GR712RC processors. The GR740 radiation-hardened quad-core LEON4FT processor serves as the computing engine for the Wildcat Processor Card, used in the spacecraft’s primary and redundant Command and Data Handling systems as well as the Instrument Command and Data Handling systems for both the Wide Field Instrument and Coronagraph Instrument.

Operating at up to 250 MHz, the GR740 provides the fault-tolerant processing capability required for one of NASA’s most advanced science missions. Roman’s Science Data Recorder also uses Frontgrade Gaisler’s GR712RC radiation-hardened dual-core LEON3FT processor to support the storage and management of scientific data generated by the observatory’s instruments.

NASA’s Goddard Space Flight Center developed the Wildcat Processor Card as a core element of Roman’s avionics architecture. Flight-qualified units supported spacecraft and instrument integration, verification, and testing on the GR740-based computing platform.

“Roman is a powerful example of what international collaboration and trusted technology can enable in space,” said Sandi Habinc, General Manager, Frontgrade Gaisler. “The GR740 began as a European Space Agency and Swedish National Space Agency investment in next-generation space processing and is now supporting a flagship NASA science mission. We are proud to see that European heritage combined with Frontgrade’s broader space electronics capabilities to help enable a mission of this significance.”

The GR740 was developed as the European Space Agency’s next-generation microprocessor and has achieved Technology Readiness Level 9. Together with the flight-proven GR712RC, it provides scalable, radiation-hardened processing for scientific, exploration, government, and commercial space missions.

Frontgrade’s role on Roman extends beyond onboard processing. The observatory also incorporates Frontgrade radiation-hardened microelectronics, including quad NAND gates, quad OR gates, transceivers, and voltage supervisors. These devices support communications, power management, control logic and fault-tolerant operation throughout the spacecraft. Together, these technologies illustrate the increasingly integrated electronics architectures required for advanced space missions. Processing, memory, communications, power management, and other critical functions must work together within demanding size, power, reliability and radiation constraints. Frontgrade supports that architecture with technologies spanning mission processing, microelectronics, RF and other mission-critical spacecraft systems.

“The Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is not only a milestone for astronomy, but also a powerful demonstration of the value of long-term investment in advanced space technology. We are particularly proud to see the GR740, a processor developed through ESA programmes and European industrial excellence, performing mission-critical functions aboard. The use of our components highlights Europe's ability to deliver world-class technologies that enable some of the most ambitious scientific missions of our time. This is precisely why ESA continues to invest in strategic technologies that strengthen Europe's competitiveness, sovereignty and contribution to global space exploration,” said Dr Dietmar Pilz, Director of Technology, Engineering and Quality, ESA.

“We are immensely proud to see Swedish space technology contributing to NASA’s Roman Space Telescope. Frontgrade Gaisler demonstrates the world class expertise of Sweden’s space sector and the value of long-term investment and international cooperation. It is also a powerful example of how our investments through ESA drive technology development that enables Swedish companies to contribute to some of the world’s most ambitious space missions,” said Dr Ella Carlsson, Director General, SNSA.

Roman features a 2.4-meter primary mirror and a wide-field infrared camera designed to survey large regions of the sky with unprecedented efficiency. Scientists expect the observatory to advance research in dark energy, dark matter, galaxy evolution, and exoplanets while also demonstrating advanced direct-imaging technologies through its Coronagraph Instrument.

Across mission processing, microelectronics, RF systems, and motion control, Frontgrade technologies help customers sense, process, store, communicate, power and act in demanding environments where reliability is essential.

data.title: Fed's Cook says rate hikes needed to lower high inflation
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook on Friday made a case for more interest rate hikes, saying the US central bank's current policy rate is not high enough to deal with inflation levels she views with "great concern."

"In a different environment, the (Federal Open Market) Committee could afford to be patient, but I continue to believe that in this economic climate we do not have that luxury," given how high inflation is and for how long it has been above the Fed's 2% target, Cook said in the text of a speech to be presented at a central bank conference in Chile.

Cook said the quarter-percentage-point rate hike the Fed delivered at its September 15-16 policy meeting was not enough to moderate current levels of inflation.

What's more, "inflation data received since the September rate increase, including reports last week, fail to provide me with sufficient evidence that inflation is returning to a sustainable path," she said. "There is little evidence inflation is declining."

Cook, who voted for a rate hike at that meeting, was one of two Fed officials who dissented over the Fed's decision last month to leave its policy rate in the 3.75%-4.00% range. Officials at the October 27-28 meeting signaled that inflation remained too high then even as they refrained from action.

Regarding her dissent in October, Cook said, "My vote reflected the urgency I feel to tackle inflation," which "has been above target for more than five and a half years, and every additional day poses greater risk that price- and wage-setters will adjust their inflation expectations upward."

RATE HIKE EXPECTED IN DECEMBER

A wide range of Fed officials in recent weeks have signaled support for more rate hikes, and financial markets broadly expect the Fed to raise rates at its December 8-9 meeting and to follow that move with more increases next year.

Most Fed officials have made a case for gradual action to lower inflation, arguing that doing so would give the economy time to adjust to the rise in borrowing costs. But some, concerned with the most recent inflation data, have speculated that aggressive moves may be needed to bring price pressures to heel.

Cook on Friday said the risk of not acting fast enough to lower inflation could bring more pain later.

"Waiting longer to implement rate increases risks getting behind the curve," she said. "If we fall behind, additional and larger rate increases may be required later to catch up, which could increase stress on our financial system and have unnecessarily damaging effects on American households."

The Fed governor noted that financial conditions remain accommodative and are not providing the needed level of restraint on the economy.

Cook, however, was upbeat on the economy. She said growth is "strong and accelerating" and that the job market remains "solid."

(Reporting by Michael S. Derby; Editing by Paul Simao)

data.title: Anthropic's IPO bank closed position meant to stabilize stock, removing source of support
data.description:
Nov 20 (Reuters) - Anthropic's underwriter, tasked with stabilizing its share price after its market debut, closed a position meant to do that, Anthropic said on Friday. With the AI company's shares falling 11%, the move means one potential source of buying support is now unavailable. 

Anthropic named investment bank Morgan Stanley ( MS ) as the initial public offering's stabilization agent to support the stock after its market debut. In that role, the bank received an option, known as a greenshoe, to buy additional shares - 147 million in Anthropic's case - directly from the company on behalf of the underwriting syndicate. 

Alternatively, the underwriters can buy shares in the open market to cover the greenshoe, which can support the stock price. In the case of Anthropic, whose shares closed on Thursday at $97.17, about 17% above its IPO price, Morgan Stanley ( MS ) exercised the full greenshoe at the IPO price, Anthropic said. The stock was last down 11.5% on Friday at $86, after falling to as low as $85 earlier in the session.

The exercise brought aggregate gross proceeds from the IPO to roughly $93.5 billion.

Underwriters typically have up to 30 days after an IPO to exercise the greenshoe option, which allows them to buy additional shares directly from the company to cover shares sold in excess of the original offering.

It is common for underwriters to exercise the greenshoe when shares are trading above their IPO price on the first day of trading, as they can buy the additional shares directly from the company at the offering price. With the full option exercised, Morgan Stanley ( MS ) can no longer use open-market purchases to cover any remaining overallotment if shares fall below the $83 IPO price. Market participants have questioned the underwriters' timing given Thursday's market volatility, one person familiar with the matter said.

Morgan Stanley ( MS ) declined to comment.

Carsten Hesse, London-based head of index events at Berenberg, said the development is positive for Anthropic as it increases the proceeds raised in the IPO."However, it is less positive for investors, who are losing an important potential source of buying support," he said in a note to clients. "It seems like the bookrunners have given up their remaining stabilisation option already after 1 day just as the share price is getting closer to the IPO price."

Anthropic's IPO roadshow and strong market debut raised hopes that other AI companies could follow it to the public markets, with issuers looking to capitalize on renewed investor appetite. SB Energy, a company that develops, owns and operates data centers and power infrastructure, updated its IPO prospectus with the latest financial information shortly after Anthropic priced its offering, underscoring how companies were preparing to move ahead. But that optimism was tested late on Thursday as a broader selloff in technology stocks gathered pace.

data.title: Taiwan's Stock Pickers Are Walking Out to Bet Their Own Money
data.description:
NEW YORK, Oct. 19, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Fly On Wall Street News Commentary - Taiwan's benchmark stock index was up 62% this year, the best showing of any major equity gauge in the world, when Bloomberg reported on Oct. 16 that some of the island's professional fund managers and analysts are quitting their jobs to invest their own money. Strict rules keep them from trading the very stocks they pick for clients, and in a year when about one in ten stocks in the index has more than doubled, some have decided the trade-off is no longer worth it. Companies and funds mentioned in this article include: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company Limited ( TSM ) [TSMC] , ASE Technology Holding Co., Ltd. ( ASX ) [ASE] , United Microelectronics Corporation ( UMC ) [UMC] , iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF , The Taiwan Fund, Inc. ( TWN ) .

Watching From Behind the Locker

Taiwan does not ban personal investing outright, but its asset-management code of conduct bars staff from trading a locally listed stock or a linked derivative within seven business days before or after their firm's funds trade it, which in practice rules out personal stock-picking. Fund managers must also lock away their phones, laptops and smartwatches each morning until the market closes at 1:30 p.m. The phone rule was formalized in 2024 to deter insider trading, the Taipei Times reported in July, after six former fund managers from four firms were indicted for front-running trades through the accounts of relatives and friends.

Ken Tsai, 40, a fund manager who until July worked at a large Taiwanese asset manager that Bloomberg did not name, told Bloomberg he made a Taiwanese maker of AI-server data-transfer components his fund's largest holding in 2024. The stock rose more than fivefold in 2025 and about sixfold again this year, but he owned none of it personally. "It left me with a strong sense of relative deprivation," he said. He now works at a private investment firm in Taipei, which was also not named. Pay adds to the pull: Taiwan portfolio managers earn roughly US$124,000 to US$311,000 a year, well below Hong Kong base salaries, according to Bloomberg, citing headhunters and recruitment-firm data.

The private shops they are joining sit outside those rules. They register as private companies with the Ministry of Economic Affairs and do not need asset-management licenses from the Financial Supervisory Commission because they do not raise public money. Brokers told Bloomberg some of them now generate more than NT$10 billion in monthly trading volume, rivaling mid-sized asset managers.

The Rally Behind the Exits

Much of the rally traces back to the AI hardware supply chain. TSMC reported third-quarter revenue of NT$1.49 trillion (US$46.7 billion) on Oct. 15, up 50.9% from a year earlier, while net income jumped 68.7% and gross margin reached 66.4%. It guided fourth-quarter revenue from US$52.3 billion to US$54.3 billion.

Chip packaging and testing has ridden the same wave. ASE Technology ( ASX ) reported September net revenue of NT$88.1 billion, up 45.5% from a year earlier, and third-quarter revenue of NT$244.2 billion, up 44.8%.

Mature-node foundry UMC reported August sales up 30.71% from a year earlier, lifting year-to-date sales 14.66%. In its second-quarter report, the company guided for capacity utilization above 90% in the third quarter and said revenue from its 22/28nm business continues to set record highs.

CONTINUED... Read more market coverage at: flyonwallstreet.com

A Talent Squeeze, Not a Stampede

The numbers point to churn more than an exodus. Fewer than half of Taiwan's 20 largest local equity mutual funds have kept the same portfolio manager for more than three years, according to fund-data site MoneyDJ, and Bloomberg reported that applications for junior roles at some international firms have roughly halved this year. Yet the FSC said the industry's registered headcount actually rose to 4,729 in September from 4,581 at the end of 2025. Firms are responding: the largest foreign asset manager in Taiwan is offering cross-market analyst roles and office rotations to keep staff.

Regulators are paying attention. The FSC said on Oct. 15 it is gathering information and plans to review the rules, balancing market development against conflicts of interest and investor protection. One asset-management executive told Bloomberg there is no easy solution for now.

The Case for the Pros

At least one professionally managed fund has kept pace. The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ), a closed-end fund listed in New York, reported a 47.36% total return for its fiscal quarter ended May 31, against 26.12% for the TAIEX Total Return Index over the same period, with net asset value of US$116.90 a share at the end of that quarter.

Investors who prefer to own the whole market can use the iShares MSCI Taiwan ETF, which holds about US$11.9 billion in assets.

Last week was a reminder of how quickly the math can change. The TAIEX fell 4.6%, its first weekly decline in five weeks, as a technology selloff spread and TSMC CEO C.C. Wei warned of macroeconomic uncertainty and weak consumer demand, according to Trading Economics. In New York, TSMC's shares fell 8.98% from the Oct. 9 close to $412.61 on Oct. 16, ASE dropped 14.86% to $39.53, UMC slid 13.68% to $19.82, the iShares fund lost 7.04% to $106.26 and The Taiwan Fund ( TWN ) declined 8.78% to $94.18, according to Stock Analysis data. For the managers who just traded a salary for their own account, those swings now land on them.

data.title: Trump, Xi agreed that military AI decisions should involve humans, Bessent says
data.description:
* Agreement requires human involvement in major military actions using AI, Bessent says

* Spying allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang did not arise in Trump-Xi meeting, Bessent says

* Nvidia's ( NVDA ) H200 remains most advanced AI chip China can buy with licenses, Bessent says

By David Lawder and Doina Chiacu

WASHINGTON, Nov 20 (Reuters) - US President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping agreed humans should always be involved in military decisions that use artificial intelligence technologies, even as the two countries compete for AI supremacy, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday.

Bessent told CNBC after returning from Trump's meeting with Xi in Shenzhen, China, that the agreement was among the major achievements of Trump's trip to Asia.

"I think it was very important that President Trump and President Xi agreed that humans should always be involved in any military decisions that SI make makes, and the SI should not be allowed to be autonomous for major military actions," Bessent said, referring to the Trump administration's preferred term for the technology, "super intelligence."

Bessent said that the US-China agreement on military use of the technology, requiring human involvement and other safeguards, would not be affected by the two countries' competition for AI supremacy. He added that US AI labs needed to maintain their technological lead as the best defense against "dangerous" Chinese AI models that are being used in cyberattacks.

"But there's nothing to do with competition when it says that both sides agree that no major military operation should be launched without a human being involved," Bessent said.

He said that the spying allegations involving former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a Chinese national that he was romantically involved with did not come up in the Trump-Xi bilateral meeting.

Bessent said that Nvidia's ( NVDA ) second tier AI chip, the H200, remained the most advanced chip that China could purchase with licenses, after Trump took what he called a "very firm line."

"I think what we have seen is a paucity of orders from the Chinese on the H200s as they try to build out their own chip stack, and I think that they are probably many years behind," he added.

Bessent downplayed differences that he had voiced between the views of Treasury and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick on AI chip restrictions in the wake of the Nvidia scandal, saying Trump administration officials were "all committed to following President Trump's instructions."

The Commerce Department took steps on Monday to further restrict China's access to advanced AI chips, including those used by overseas data centers where Chinese entities can rent computing power.

"I think we are going to see that the proper chip restrictions are in place, the and the remote access has been curtailed," he said.

(Reporting by David Lawder; Editing by Doina Chiacu and Sanjeev Miglani)
